A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PropInfer and the same two property-inference attacks. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: V3 reports original gender and medical-diagnosis inference experiments, target-model evaluations and attack ablations across three LLM families.

after.justification: V4 retains these empirical results and adds keyword correlations, model-transfer testing and temperature-defense experiments.

M1.justification: The two attack procedures remain unchanged. Section 7 and Appendix A.4 introduce an implemented defense that changes output-sampling temperature, replacing v3's untested reweighting suggestion. The corrected loss formulas do not establish a change to the implemented training procedure.

E1.justification: ChatDoctor gender and diagnosis tasks, Q&A and chat-completion modes, Alpaca instruction tuning and iCliniq evaluation remain unchanged. Added experiments vary model pairings and decoding settings within existing coverage. News datasets are mentioned only as future work.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparator sets retain direct asking, perplexity and generation without fine-tuning in their corresponding benchmark comparisons. Newly reported pretrained gender ratios support a bias analysis; the newly cited membership-inference methods are not evaluated as additional attack baselines.

E3.justification: Existing experimental settings are retained. New protocols test Llama-3 shadow models against a Llama-1 target and evaluate Llama-3 chat-completion decoding temperatures of 0.5, 1, 1.5 and 3.5 across the existing three female ratios.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained hyperparameter and prompt ablations, v4 adds quantitative keyword associations, pretraining-bias analysis, a test relaxing knowledge of the target's pretrained model, and the first empirical defense study. This substantially extends supplementary evaluation to attack-assumption robustness and mitigation.

E5.justification: Tables 3 and 7 introduce explicit correlation-coefficient estimation and reporting for keyword frequencies versus female ratios, replacing purely qualitative association examples. Existing seed counts and uncertainty displays remain unchanged; the new transfer and defense tables provide no uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: The original benchmark tables, BERTScore results, prompt results and ablation plots are unchanged. V4 adds pretrained gender ratios, keyword correlations, transfer MAEs and temperature-dependent predictions. Its new Section 6.2 summary of 17.5% Llama-1 Q&A MAE does not match the approximately 17.81% average of Table 1's three entries.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 corrects the pretraining, SFT and CLM-FT objectives from the negative logarithm of summed token probabilities to the negative sum of token log probabilities. This repairs mathematically different expressions while retaining the stated negative-log-likelihood interpretation. No new proofs or theorems appear.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central contributions: PropInfer, two tailored attacks, dataset-level confidentiality leakage and dependence on fine-tuning mode. Added analyses support these claims without changing their central scope.

C2.justification: V4 adds explanations involving pretraining bias, rare keyword signals and model-transfer sensitivity. It introduces temperature-defense failure conditions and explicitly identifies evaluation outside medical data as future work. The principal memorization and childbirth interpretations remain.

D1.justification: V4 adds a code-access link in the abstract, fuller selected-keyword lists and concrete defense settings. Hardware, LoRA hyperparameters, labeling instructions, prompts and dataset-access information are retained; experimental setup moves from Appendix A.4 to A.2.

R1.justification: V4 adds Kaneko et al. on sampling-based pseudo-likelihood and Meeus et al. on synthetic-text privacy auditing. Section 5.2 replaces its unqualified description of word frequency as a new feature with acknowledgment of parallel membership-inference research.

P1.justification: V4 locally rewrites the results discussion, expands Section 6.3 into Additional studies, consolidates setup and perplexity details in Appendix A.2, and adds acknowledgments and a defense subsection. Most introductory and methodological prose remains intact.

P2.justification: V4 adds keyword tables 3 and 7, model-transfer Table 4 and defense Table 9. Existing tables and figures are relocated or renumbered, including the prompt table becoming Table 8. All original figures retain their content and the overall layout remains similar.

improvement.justification: V4 corrects the loss formulas and improves scrutiny of the attacks through quantitative associations, model-transfer testing and an empirical defense study, while adding code-access information. These are useful but limited gains: the new tests are narrow, lack uncertainty and defended-model utility evaluation, and introduce a small MAE-summary inconsistency. The original benchmark evidence remains intact.
